explanation: For rational α ∈ (0,1) the formal statement asserts a sentence φ whose probability under G(n, n^{-α}) converges to no b ∈ [0, ∞], i.e. failure of the convergence law, which is stronger than failure of the 0-1 law. This stronger form is what Shelah–Spencer proved: Zhukovskii et al. (arXiv:2402.02567, §1) state 'Shelah and Spencer disproved even the FO convergence law for G(n, n^{-α}) when α ∈ (0,1) is rational'. Faithful.
